title: Export DSL output to glTF/GLB for Blender and game engines
description: Export the DSL's result in a form Blender or a game engine reads. Today the only writers are the private writeObj helpers in ValidateDsl and BatchDslEvaluator. Add a public GltfMeshWriter in geometry/mesh/data/load (the inverse of CRAW-1's parser), an `export_mesh(geometry, path, format="glb")` node, and `ixdar-cli mesh-export --path out.glb`. The GLB carries: triangle (or quad-triangulated) mesh with normals; the UV slot and MaterialData as a PBR metallic-roughness material with embedded PNG textures (CRAW-3, multi-material from CRAW-14 as multiple primitives); _bone_weight_* slots as a skin (JOINTS_0/WEIGHTS_0, joints and inverse bind matrices from apply_bone); patch labels (CRAW-6) as per-label primitives or `_LABEL_<name>` custom vertex attributes so Blender shows them as vertex groups; the label hierarchy in `extras`. Output must be byte-stable (sorted maps; the Map.of salting trap). Verify with a headless Blender import script.
definition-of-done: 1. export_mesh writes a valid GLB (passes glTF-Validator or a python `pygltflib` load) for cube, hand.dsl, and a textured crawfish scan. 2. Blender headless (`blender -b --python check_glb.py -- out.glb`) imports it and reports expected vertex/face counts, materials with textures, an armature with the expected bone names, and vertex groups per label. 3. Round trip: export then load through CRAW-1 yields the same `mesh-fingerprint`. 4. Two exports of the same bundle are byte-identical. 5. `ixdar-cli mesh-export` documented via gen-docs. 6. Build checkstyle-green.
testing-plan: 1. Unit: GltfMeshWriterTest writes a two-triangle bundle with UVs and one bone; parse back with the CRAW-1 parser and compare. 2. Byte-stability test (two writes, equal bytes). 3. Blender headless script in tools/ asserting the imported structure on hand.dsl output. 4. CLI: `mesh-export` against a running mesh-viewer; validate the file.
